components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 客人从前门进来了。
example.pinyin: Kèrén cóng qiánmén jìnlái le.
example.english: The guest came in through the front door.
example.fact: The oldest surviving wooden door in Europe, found at a Neolithic lake settlement near Zurich, Switzerland, has been dated to around 3063 BC and still has its original wooden pivot hinges intact. Archaeologists believe it once sealed the entrance to a stilt house built over the water.

examples.hanzi: 前门有点堵,请从后门进去吧。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmén yǒudiǎn dǔ, qǐng cóng hòumén jìnqù ba.
examples.english: The front door is a bit blocked, so please go in through the back door.

examples.hanzi: 公交车的乘客从前门上车。
examples.pinyin: Gōngjiāochē de chéngkè cóng qiánmén shàngchē.
examples.english: Bus passengers board through the front door.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; tallies were bamboo slips split in two to match, so 符 is to match.
付 (fù) — near sound — 符 is fú; 付 also sounds out 附 fù and 府 fǔ.

example.hanzi: 他的说法与证据相符。
example.pinyin: Tā de shuōfǎ yǔ zhèngjù xiāngfú.
example.english: His statement matches the evidence.
example.fact: In his 1892 book Finger Prints, Francis Galton showed that fingerprint patterns are distinctive enough that no two individuals, not even identical twins, had ever been found to share the same one. That work laid the statistical groundwork for using fingerprints to match suspects to crime scenes.

examples.hanzi: 你说的话和事实不相符。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de huà hé shìshí bù xiāngfú.
examples.english: What you said doesn't match the facts.

examples.hanzi: 照片上的人和本人很相符。
examples.pinyin: Zhàopiàn shàng de rén hé běnrén hěn xiāngfú.
examples.english: The person in the photo matches the real person well.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water, as in 海 sea, 河 river; 湾 is a bay, where water curves in.
弯 (wān) — same sound and also means curved: 湾 is a curve in the coast.

example.hanzi: 这个海湾很漂亮。
example.pinyin: Zhège hǎiwān hěn piàoliang.
example.english: This bay is very beautiful.
example.fact: 湾 is a bay: 海湾, 港湾. 台湾 (Taiwan) literally means "terrace bay." 湾区 means a bay area, and 粤港澳大湾区 is the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area.

examples.hanzi: 渔船都停在海湾里。
examples.pinyin: Yúchuán dōu tíng zài hǎiwān lǐ.
examples.english: The fishing boats are all anchored in the bay.

examples.hanzi: 台湾是一个美丽的地方。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān shì yí ge měilì de dìfang.
examples.english: Taiwan is a beautiful place.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 萤火虫在夜里发光。
example.pinyin: Yínghuǒchóng zài yèlǐ fāguāng.
example.english: Fireflies glow at night.
example.fact: Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction between a molecule called luciferin and the enzyme luciferase inside specialized cells in their abdomens. The reaction converts chemical energy into light with almost none lost as heat, making it far more energy-efficient than an incandescent bulb.

examples.hanzi: 夜里,海面上的小虫在发光。
examples.pinyin: Yèlǐ, hǎimiàn shàng de xiǎochóng zài fāguāng.
examples.english: At night, little creatures on the sea surface glow.

examples.hanzi: 这个手环会发光,晚上跑步很安全。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒuhuán huì fāguāng, wǎnshang pǎobù hěn ānquán.
examples.english: This wristband glows, so running at night is safe.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 他从英格兰来到中国留学。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng Yīnggélán láidào Zhōngguó liúxué.
example.english: He came from England to study in China.
example.fact: Stonehenge, in southern England, was built in stages starting around 3000 BC, and some of its smaller bluestones were quarried in the Preseli Hills of Wales, more than 200 kilometers away. How Neolithic builders transported multi-ton stones that far, without wheels or draft animals, is still debated by archaeologists.

examples.hanzi: 他的英格兰口音很重。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Yīnggélán kǒuyīn hěn zhòng.
examples.english: He has a strong English accent.

examples.hanzi: 英格兰足球队今天晚上有比赛。
examples.pinyin: Yīnggélán zúqiúduì jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu bǐsài.
examples.english: The England football team has a match tonight.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 泳 is swimming.
永 (yǒng) — same sound — 泳 is yǒng, like 永; 永 also sounds out 咏 yǒng.
氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 湖; 池 is a pond.
也 (yě) hints at the sound: 池 chí is close to 驰 chí and 弛 chí.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在泳池里玩耍。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài yǒngchí lǐ wánshuǎ.
example.english: The children are playing in the swimming pool.
example.fact: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BC in the Indus Valley Civilization, is one of the earliest known public water tanks, with a brick-lined basin, waterproof mortar, and its own drainage system. Its exact purpose — ritual bathing, public use, or both — is still debated by archaeologists.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我们常去小区的泳池游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒmen cháng qù xiǎoqū de yǒngchí yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer we often swim in the neighborhood pool.

examples.hanzi: 这个泳池每天早上八点开放。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yǒngchí měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn kāifàng.
examples.english: This swimming pool opens at eight every morning.

meanings: see 恆星系|恒星系[heng2 xing1 xi4]

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.

example.hanzi: 银河系只是宇宙中众多星系之一。
example.pinyin: Yínhéxì zhǐshì yǔzhòu zhōng zhòngduō xīngxì zhī yī.
example.english: The Milky Way is just one of many galaxies in the universe.
example.fact: Estimates of how many galaxies exist have grown sharply as telescopes improved: analysis of deep Hubble Space Telescope images published in 2016 suggested the observable universe may contain roughly two trillion galaxies, about ten times higher than earlier estimates. Most of those galaxies are too faint or distant to be seen with current instruments.

examples.hanzi: 天文学家发现了一个新的星系。
examples.pinyin: Tiānwénxuéjiā fāxiànle yí gè xīn de xīngxì.
examples.english: Astronomers discovered a new galaxy.

examples.hanzi: 这个星系离地球非常遥远。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīngxì lí dìqiú fēicháng yáoyuǎn.
examples.english: This galaxy is extremely far from the Earth.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警方终于结案了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhōngyú jié'àn le.
example.english: The police finally closed the case.
example.fact: The Golden State Killer case went unsolved for more than 40 years until 2018, when investigators uploaded DNA from an old crime scene sample to a public genealogy website and traced it through distant relatives to Joseph James DeAngelo. The technique, now called forensic genetic genealogy, has since helped close dozens of other cold cases.

examples.hanzi: 这起案子已经结案,不用再查了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànzi yǐjīng jié'àn, bú yòng zài chá le.
examples.english: This case is closed and doesn't need further investigation.

examples.hanzi: 法官宣布案件将在下周结案。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān xuānbù ànjiàn jiāng zài xiàzhōu jié'àn.
examples.english: The judge announced that the case will be closed next week.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
又 (right hand) — a hand with a dot between the fingers, the idea of a fork or crossing; also in 友 friend, 取 take.

example.hanzi: 两条路在这里交叉。
example.pinyin: Liǎng tiáo lù zài zhèlǐ jiāochā.
example.english: The two roads cross here.
example.fact: The first cloverleaf highway interchange in the United States was built in 1928 near Woodbridge, New Jersey, using looping ramps so that crossing roads could merge and diverge without a single traffic light. The design spread rapidly once the interstate highway system began construction in the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 这两条线在中间交叉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng tiáo xiàn zài zhōngjiān jiāochā.
examples.english: These two lines cross in the middle.

examples.hanzi: 我们的工作时间有点交叉,很难见面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de gōngzuò shíjiān yǒudiǎn jiāochā, hěn nán jiànmiàn.
examples.english: Our work hours overlap a bit, so it's hard to meet.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.

example.hanzi: 这根线很细。
example.pinyin: Zhè gēn xiàn hěn xì.
example.english: This thread is very thin.
example.fact: 细 is the opposite of 粗 and describes thin round things like thread or legs; flat things like paper use 薄. It also means careful and detailed: 仔细, 细心, 细节 (detail), 细菌 (bacteria).

examples.hanzi: 这支笔写出来的字很细。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī bǐ xiě chūlái de zì hěn xì.
examples.english: The writing from this pen is very thin.

examples.hanzi: 请你把情况仔细说一遍。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bǎ qíngkuàng zǐxì shuō yí biàn.
examples.english: Please explain the situation carefully once more.

components.note: 元 (first, head) — a person with the head marked: 元 first meant the head, so first, chief, origin. 元 also gives 完 wán, 玩 wán and 院 yuàn.
首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.

example.hanzi: 两国元首举行了会谈。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó yuánshǒu jǔxíng le huìtán.
example.english: The heads of the two states held talks.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II served as the United Kingdom's head of state for over 70 years, from 1952 to 2022, the longest verified reign of any female monarch in recorded history. Her reign spanned 15 British prime ministers, starting with Winston Churchill.

examples.hanzi: 各国元首都出席了开幕式。
examples.pinyin: Gèguó yuánshǒu dōu chūxíle kāimù shì.
examples.english: Heads of state from all countries attended the opening ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 电视上正在播放元首的新年讲话。
examples.pinyin: Diànshì shàng zhèngzài bōfàng yuánshǒu de xīnnián jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The head of state's New Year address is being broadcast on TV.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.hanzi: 尊重每个人的意愿很重要。
example.pinyin: Zūnzhòng měi gèrén de yìyuàn hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: It's important to respect everyone's wishes.
example.fact: The 1947 Nuremberg Code, drafted after wartime medical atrocities were exposed at the Nuremberg trials, established that voluntary consent from research subjects is essential before any experiment can proceed. It became the founding document behind modern medical ethics rules on patient autonomy and informed consent.

examples.hanzi: 这完全是我自己的意愿,没人逼我。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wánquán shì wǒ zìjǐ de yìyuàn, méi rén bī wǒ.
examples.english: This is entirely my own wish; nobody forced me.

examples.hanzi: 他有去国外工作的意愿。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu qù guówài gōngzuò de yìyuàn.
examples.english: He is willing to work abroad.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.

example.hanzi: 电子邮件逐渐取代了传统信件。
example.pinyin: Diànzǐ yóujiàn zhújiàn qǔdài le chuántǒng xìnjiàn.
example.english: Email has gradually replaced traditional letters.
example.fact: Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first working digital camera prototype in 1975, but the company was slow to commercialize the technology it had invented, fearing it would undercut film sales. Digital cameras eventually replaced film almost entirely, and Kodak filed for bankruptcy protection in 2012.

examples.hanzi: 很多人觉得机器人会取代人类的工作。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén juéde jīqìrén huì qǔdài rénlèi de gōngzuò.
examples.english: Many people think robots will replace human jobs.

examples.hanzi: 新来的老师取代了原来的班主任。
examples.pinyin: Xīn lái de lǎoshī qǔdàile yuánlái de bānzhǔrèn.
examples.english: The new teacher replaced the original homeroom teacher.

components.note: 刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 医生切除了病人的肿瘤。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng qiēchú le bìngrén de zhǒngliú.
example.english: The doctor removed the patient's tumor.
example.fact: On October 16, 1846, surgeon John Collins Warren removed a tumor from a patient's neck at Massachusetts General Hospital while dentist William Morton administered ether gas, in what became known as the Ether Dome demonstration. It was one of the first public surgeries performed with general anesthesia, transforming surgery from an agonizing ordeal into a painless procedure.

examples.hanzi: 医生说需要切除这颗坏牙。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō xūyào qiēchú zhè kē huài yá.
examples.english: The doctor said this bad tooth needs to be removed.

examples.hanzi: 手术中,他们切除了一部分胃。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushù zhōng, tāmen qiēchúle yí bùfen wèi.
examples.english: During the surgery, they removed part of his stomach.

components.note: 目 (eye) — eyes and seeing: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball; sleep is when the eyes close.
垂 (chuí, droop) hints at the sound and the image: drooping eyelids. Also in 锤 chuí.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 她穿着睡衣看电视。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe shuìyī kàn diànshì.
example.english: She is watching TV in her pajamas.
example.fact: Unlike most primates, which sleep in several short bouts scattered across the day and night, humans consolidate sleep into a single long block. Some researchers link this shift to our ancestors' controlled use of fire and shelter, which made it safer to sleep deeply through the night rather than stay half-alert against predators.

examples.hanzi: 这件睡衣又软又舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shuìyī yòu ruǎn yòu shūfu.
examples.english: This pair of pajamas is soft and comfortable.

examples.hanzi: 孩子穿着睡衣跑到了客厅。
examples.pinyin: Háizi chuānzhe shuìyī pǎodàole kètīng.
examples.english: The child ran into the living room in pajamas.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.

example.hanzi: 卫星接收到了地面信号。
example.pinyin: Wèixīng jiēshōu dào le dìmiàn xìnhào.
example.english: The satellite received the signal from the ground.
example.fact: When the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in October 1957, the satellite transmitted a simple radio beep that amateur radio operators around the world could pick up on ordinary shortwave receivers. That beep, audible to the public within hours of launch, is widely credited with kicking off the space age.

examples.hanzi: 请及时接收我发给你的文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí jiēshōu wǒ fā gěi nǐ de wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please receive the file I sent you in time.

examples.hanzi: 这所学校接收了很多外国留学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào jiēshōule hěn duō wàiguó liúxuéshēng.
examples.english: This school has accepted many international students.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 警方保存了现场的证物。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng bǎocún le xiànchǎng de zhèngwù.
example.english: The police preserved the evidence from the scene.
example.fact: In 1988, Colin Pitchfork became the first person convicted of murder using DNA profiling, a technique developed a few years earlier by geneticist Alec Jeffreys at the University of Leicester. The same method also cleared an initial suspect who had falsely confessed to the crime, showing DNA evidence could exonerate as well as convict.

examples.hanzi: 这把刀是重要的证物,不能随便碰。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo shì zhòngyào de zhèngwù, bù néng suíbiàn pèng.
examples.english: This knife is important evidence and can't be touched carelessly.

examples.hanzi: 法庭上,律师出示了几件证物。
examples.pinyin: Fǎtíng shàng, lǜshī chūshìle jǐ jiàn zhèngwù.
examples.english: In court, the lawyer presented several pieces of evidence.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a gloomy feeling; also in 想 think, 急 anxious.
门 (mén) gives a close sound; 们 men shares it. 闷 reads mēn (stuffy) or mèn (gloomy).

example.hanzi: 屋里太闷了，开窗吧。
example.pinyin: Wū lǐ tài mēn le, kāi chuāng ba.
example.english: It is stuffy in the room, so open the window.
example.fact: 闷 has two readings: mēn is physically stuffy (闷热 muggy, 闷在家里 stuck at home), and mèn is a gloomy feeling (烦闷, 郁闷 depressed). Colloquially, 闷得慌 means "bored or oppressed."

examples.hanzi: 他心情不好，一个人闷在家里。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīnqíng bù hǎo, yí ge rén mēn zài jiālǐ.
examples.english: He is in a bad mood and keeps himself cooped up at home.

examples.hanzi: 我今天心里有点烦闷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān xīnlǐ yǒudiǎn fánmèn.
examples.english: I feel a bit gloomy today.

components.note: 饣 (food; traditional 食) — marks food and eating, as in 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饺 dumpling; 饶 is abundant, with plenty to eat, as in 丰饶; also to forgive 饶恕.
尧 (yáo) — close sound: 饶 ráo. 尧 also sounds out 烧 shāo and 晓 xiǎo.

example.hanzi: 这次饶了你，下次不行。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì ráo le nǐ, xià cì bù xíng.
example.english: I'll let you off this time, but not next time.
example.fact: 饶 means to spare or forgive: 饶恕, 求饶 (to beg for mercy), 饶命 (spare my life). In shops it can mean to add something free: 饶你一个. 富饶 means rich and abundant, and 饶舌 is the Chinese term for rap music.

examples.hanzi: 这次就饶了他吧，他已经道歉了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì jiù ráo le tā ba, tā yǐjīng dàoqiàn le.
examples.english: Let him off this time. He has already apologized.

examples.hanzi: 老板人很好，还饶了我们一份甜点。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn rén hěn hǎo, hái ráo le wǒmen yí fèn tiándiǎn.
examples.english: The owner is nice and even threw in a dessert for us.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
心 (heart) — feelings and thinking: 想 think, 思, 感 feel, 忙; forgetting is a loss of the heart's hold.
亡 (wáng, lose) gives the sound and fits the sense: to lose from the mind.

example.hanzi: 时间让人渐渐遗忘痛苦。
example.pinyin: Shíjiān ràng rén jiànjiàn yíwàng tòngkǔ.
example.english: Time gradually makes people forget pain.
example.fact: In the 1880s, psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus memorized lists of nonsense syllables and tested his own recall over time, finding that memory for new information drops sharply within the first hours after learning before leveling off. His results, later called the forgetting curve, remain a foundational finding in memory research.

examples.hanzi: 有些事情,我希望能早点遗忘。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē shìqing, wǒ xīwàng néng zǎodiǎn yíwàng.
examples.english: There are some things I hope to forget soon.

examples.hanzi: 这座小镇被世界遗忘了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò xiǎozhèn bèi shìjiè yíwàng le.
examples.english: This little town has been forgotten by the world.

components.note: 刀 — the picture of a knife blade; as 刂 on the right it marks cutting, as in 别, 利, 剪.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他用刀子切水果。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng dāozi qiē shuǐguǒ.
example.english: He uses a knife to cut fruit.
example.fact: The Oldowan stone tools of East Africa, some dated to about 2.6 million years ago, are among the earliest known deliberately shaped cutting implements, made by striking flakes off a stone core to create a sharp edge. They predate the appearance of the genus Homo, suggesting even earlier hominins were capable toolmakers.

examples.hanzi: 这把刀子很锋利,小心别割到手。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāozi hěn fēnglì, xiǎoxīn bié gēdào shǒu.
examples.english: This knife is very sharp, so be careful not to cut your hand.

examples.hanzi: 厨房抽屉里有三把刀子。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng chōuti lǐ yǒu sān bǎ dāozi.
examples.english: There are three knives in the kitchen drawer.

components.note: 田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 车上有一个备用轮胎。
example.pinyin: Chē shàng yǒu yí gè bèiyòng lúntāi.
example.english: There's a spare tire in the car.
example.fact: When an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 in 1970, the crew survived partly because NASA had built backup systems into the spacecraft and mission control engineers improvised a fix, using materials on board, to adapt a square carbon dioxide scrubber to fit a round filter socket. The mission became a textbook case for designing redundancy into critical systems.

examples.hanzi: 我包里总是带着一把备用雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bāo lǐ zǒngshì dàizhe yì bǎ bèiyòng yǔsǎn.
examples.english: I always carry a spare umbrella in my bag.

examples.hanzi: 这个电话号码是备用的,你记一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diànhuà hàomǎ shì bèiyòng de, nǐ jì yíxià.
examples.english: This phone number is a backup, so make a note of it.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 谢: 该 is what one ought to say or do.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for gāi; 亥 also sounds out 孩 hái, 核 hé and 刻 kè.

example.hanzi: 这本该是一个简单的任务。
example.pinyin: Zhè běngāi shì yí gè jiǎndān de rènwù.
example.english: This was supposed to be a simple task.
example.fact: In 1847, physician Ignaz Semmelweis found that maternal deaths from childbed fever in his Vienna hospital ward dropped sharply once doctors washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients. His colleagues largely dismissed the idea, and it was only decades after his death that handwashing became standard medical practice — a delay so infamous that resistance to obvious, well-supported findings is sometimes called the Semmelweis reflex.

examples.hanzi: 你本该早点告诉我这件事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ běn gāi zǎodiǎn gàosu wǒ zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: You should have told me about this earlier.

examples.hanzi: 今天本该是个好天气,谁知下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān běn gāi shì gè hǎo tiānqì, shéi zhī xiàyǔ le.
examples.english: Today should have been nice weather, but it rained.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling or prying by hand; also in 拉 pull, 推 push.
反 (fǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn and 饭 fàn.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 他的手指放在扳机上。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ fàng zài bānjī shàng.
example.english: His finger rested on the trigger.
example.fact: Matchlock firearms, developed in 15th-century Europe, were among the first guns to use a lever mechanism to lower a lit slow-burning cord into the flash pan, automating a job that previously required the shooter to apply fire by hand at the exact moment of firing. That lever is considered an early ancestor of the modern trigger.

examples.hanzi: 他轻轻扣动了玩具枪的扳机。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng kòudòngle wánjù qiāng de bānjī.
examples.english: He lightly pulled the trigger of the toy gun.

examples.hanzi: 这把玩具枪的扳机坏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ wánjù qiāng de bānjī huài le.
examples.english: The trigger on this toy gun is broken.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).

example.hanzi: 他恐怕不会来了。
example.pinyin: Tā kǒngpà bú huì lái le.
example.english: I'm afraid he won't be coming.
example.fact: 恐 is fear: 恐惧, 恐怖 (terror), 恐龙 (dinosaur, "terrifying dragon"). 恐怕 can mean "I'm afraid that," a polite way to deliver a likely negative outcome.

examples.hanzi: 我恐怕今天没法去了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kǒngpà jīntiān méi fǎ qù le.
examples.english: I am afraid I cannot go today.

examples.hanzi: 他对高处有一点恐惧。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì gāochù yǒu yìdiǎn kǒngjù.
examples.english: He is a little afraid of heights.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.
又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.

example.hanzi: 该国严格管控枪支。
example.pinyin: Gāi guó yángé guǎnkòng qiāngzhī.
example.english: That country strictly controls guns.
example.fact: Starting in 1607, Japan's Tokugawa shogunate carried out sword and firearm confiscation edicts, known as katanagari, that sharply restricted private ownership of blades and guns for over 250 years. Historians point to that long policy as one factor behind Japan's comparatively low rates of gun ownership today.

examples.hanzi: 机场的安检会检查有没有枪支。
examples.pinyin: Jīchǎng de ānjiǎn huì jiǎnchá yǒu méiyǒu qiāngzhī.
examples.english: Airport security checks whether there are any firearms.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家不允许个人拥有枪支。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā bù yǔnxǔ gèrén yōngyǒu qiāngzhī.
examples.english: This country doesn't allow individuals to own guns.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 我们在车站分别了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn fēnbié le.
example.english: We parted ways at the station.
example.fact: Mantis shrimp have 12 to 16 types of photoreceptors in their eyes, compared to just three in humans, which in theory should let them distinguish far more categories of color. Oddly, behavioral tests suggest their brains process color more coarsely than the receptor count implies, and scientists are still debating exactly how they actually use this unusual visual system.

examples.hanzi: 我分别给他们两个人打了电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ fēnbié gěi tāmen liǎng gè rén dǎle diànhuà.
examples.english: I called the two of them separately.

examples.hanzi: 这两个词的意思很难分别。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè cí de yìsi hěn nán fēnbié.
examples.english: It's hard to tell the meanings of these two words apart.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.hanzi: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的。
example.pinyin: Měi gèrén de zhǐwén dōu shì dúyīwú'èr de.
example.english: Everyone's fingerprints are unique.
example.fact: Physicist Kenneth Libbrecht's research on snow crystals supports the popular claim that no two snowflakes are exactly alike: each crystal falls through slightly different, constantly shifting conditions of temperature and humidity, so the branching pattern that forms is shaped by an essentially unrepeatable sequence of microscopic events.

examples.hanzi: 这件手工礼物是独一无二的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shǒugōng lǐwù shì dúyī-wú'èr de.
examples.english: This handmade gift is one of a kind.

examples.hanzi: 她的声音独一无二,一听就知道是她。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn dúyī-wú'èr, yì tīng jiù zhīdào shì tā.
examples.english: Her voice is unique, and you know it's her as soon as you hear it.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees; 梅 is the plum tree, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
每 (měi) gives the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 悔 huǐ and 海 hǎi.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 梅林是亚瑟王传说中的魔法师。
example.pinyin: Méilín shì Yàsèwáng chuánshuō zhōng de mófǎshī.
example.english: Merlin is the wizard in the legend of King Arthur.
example.fact: The wizard Merlin was largely popularized by the 12th-century Welsh cleric Geoffrey of Monmouth in his Historia Regum Britanniae, written around 1136, which fused older Welsh folklore figures such as Myrddin Wyllt into the character familiar today. Later medieval writers, including Robert de Boron, expanded Merlin's role and tied him more closely to Arthur's story.

examples.hanzi: 梅林是故事里最聪明的魔法师。
examples.pinyin: Méilín shì gùshi lǐ zuì cōngmíng de mófǎshī.
examples.english: Merlin is the cleverest wizard in the story.

examples.hanzi: 这本书讲的是梅林和年轻国王的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū jiǎng de shì Méilín hé niánqīng guówáng de gùshi.
examples.english: This book tells the story of Merlin and a young king.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 这时,门突然打开了。
example.pinyin: Zhè shí, mén tūrán dǎkāi le.
example.english: At that moment, the door suddenly opened.
example.fact: Einstein's 1905 theory of special relativity showed that simultaneity is not absolute: two events that appear to happen at exactly 'this moment' for one observer can appear to happen at different times for another observer moving at a different speed. The effect is imperceptible at everyday speeds but has been confirmed repeatedly using atomic clocks on fast-moving aircraft and satellites.

examples.hanzi: 我刚想出门,这时电话响了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng xiǎng chūmén, zhèshí diànhuà xiǎng le.
examples.english: I was just about to go out when the phone rang.

examples.hanzi: 这时雨停了,太阳也出来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèshí yǔ tíng le, tàiyáng yě chūlái le.
examples.english: At this point the rain stopped and the sun came out.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 传说仙女下凡来到人间。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō xiānnǚ xiàfán láidào rénjiān.
example.english: Legend says the fairy descended to the human world.
example.fact: The world's human population passed 1 billion around 1804 and has since grown to over 8 billion, with most of that increase concentrated in just the last hundred years. That surge represents one of the fastest population expansions in the roughly 300,000-year history of our species.

examples.hanzi: 这里风景如画,像人间仙境。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ fēngjǐng rúhuà, xiàng rénjiān xiānjìng.
examples.english: The scenery here is picturesque, like a fairyland on earth.

examples.hanzi: 人间自有真情在,你不是一个人。
examples.pinyin: Rénjiān zì yǒu zhēnqíng zài, nǐ bú shì yí gè rén.
examples.english: There is true affection in this world; you're not alone.

components.note: 女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.
女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 肚 belly; 腔 is a body cavity.
空 (kōng, hollow) is a loose sound clue and fits the meaning: a hollow space.

example.hanzi: 有人说他说话有点娘娘腔。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén shuō tā shuōhuà yǒudiǎn niángniangqiāng.
example.english: Some people say he talks a bit effeminately.
example.fact: Voice pitch is set largely by the length and thickness of the vocal folds: during puberty, rising testosterone thickens the folds in most male voices, dropping pitch by roughly an octave, while the resonating spaces of the throat, mouth, and nasal cavity continue to shape each person's distinct tone. Some songbird species show the reverse pattern, developing more elaborate, higher-pitched calls as they mature in order to attract mates.

examples.hanzi: 别用“娘娘腔”这样的词笑话别人。
examples.pinyin: Bié yòng "niángniangqiāng" zhèyàng de cí xiàohua biéren.
examples.english: Don't use a word like "sissy" to mock others.

examples.hanzi: 他小时候被人说娘娘腔,心里很难受。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou bèi rén shuō niángniangqiāng, xīnlǐ hěn nánshòu.
examples.english: As a child he was called a sissy, and it hurt him deeply.

components.note: 言 (speech) — the traditional form of 讠: words and speech; an oath is a spoken promise.
折 (zhé, to break) — a promise you must not break; zhé is only a loose sound hint for shì.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 他在婚礼上说出了誓言。
example.pinyin: Tā zài hūnlǐ shàng shuōchū le shìyán.
example.english: He recited his vows at the wedding.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath is traditionally attributed to the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC, but most medical schools today swear a heavily revised modern version rather than the original text. The phrase most people associate with it, 'first, do no harm,' does not actually appear anywhere in the ancient document.

examples.hanzi: 他对妈妈发誓,会照顾好妹妹,这是他的誓言。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì māma fāshì, huì zhàogù hǎo mèimei, zhè shì tā de shìyán.
examples.english: He swore to Mom he'd look after his sister; that is his vow.

examples.hanzi: 他们牢记自己的誓言,一直没有分开。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen láojì zìjǐ de shìyán, yìzhí méiyǒu fēnkāi.
examples.english: They kept their vows in mind and have never separated.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 教练用秒表给他计时。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn yòng miǎobiǎo gěi tā jìshí.
example.english: The coach timed him with a stopwatch.
example.fact: The cesium atomic clock, built in 1955 at Britain's National Physical Laboratory, defines the second by counting oscillations of a cesium-133 atom, about 9,192,631,770 of them per second. That same precision timing underlies the GPS satellite network, which depends on atomic clocks accurate enough that even tiny errors would translate into positioning mistakes of kilometers.

examples.hanzi: 老师用手机给我们计时。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng shǒujī gěi wǒmen jìshí.
examples.english: The teacher timed us with a phone.

examples.hanzi: 考试按小时计时,时间到了必须交卷。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì àn xiǎoshí jìshí, shíjiān dào le bìxū jiāojuàn.
examples.english: The exam is timed by the hour, and papers must be handed in when time is up.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — throat and voice; also in 叫 shout, 唱 sing.
桑 (sāng) gives a close sound for sǎng.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 她的嗓音很好听。
example.pinyin: Tā de sǎngyīn hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: Her voice sounds very pleasant.
example.fact: Elephants communicate using extremely low-frequency rumbles, some below 20 Hz and inaudible to the human ear, that can travel several kilometers through the air and ground. Researchers have recorded elephants responding to these infrasound calls from herds that were far out of sight, suggesting the sounds help coordinate movement across long distances.

examples.hanzi: 他的嗓音很低,很有磁性。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sǎngyīn hěn dī, hěn yǒu cíxìng.
examples.english: His voice is deep and magnetic.

examples.hanzi: 感冒了,我今天嗓音有点哑。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnmào le, wǒ jīntiān sǎngyīn yǒudiǎn yǎ.
examples.english: I have a cold, so my voice is a bit hoarse today.

meanings: (lit.) by the thousands and tens of thousands (idiom)

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 成千上万的人参加了这次游行。
example.pinyin: Chéngqiānshàngwàn de rén cānjiā le zhè cì yóuxíng.
example.english: Thousands upon thousands of people took part in the march.
example.fact: Desert locust swarms can contain tens of billions of insects spread across hundreds of square kilometers, and a single large swarm can eat as much vegetation in a day as tens of thousands of people. Historically, such swarms have triggered famines across parts of Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia, and outbreaks are still tracked and forecast today by international monitoring agencies.

examples.hanzi: 每年成千上万的游客来到这座古城。
examples.pinyin: Měi nián chéngqiān-shàngwàn de yóukè láidào zhè zuò gǔchéng.
examples.english: Every year thousands upon thousands of tourists come to this ancient city.

examples.hanzi: 夜空中有成千上万颗星星。
examples.pinyin: Yèkōng zhōng yǒu chéngqiān-shàngwàn kē xīngxing.
examples.english: There are countless stars in the night sky.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羞 first meant offering food (a sheep dish) by hand; the sense of shame came later, as in 害羞.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings, as in 怕 afraid, 惭 ashamed; 愧 is guilt in the heart.
鬼 (guǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 魁 kuí.

example.hanzi: 他偷懒被老师发现，感到十分羞愧。
example.pinyin: tā tōulǎn bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn, gǎndào shífēn xiūkuì.
example.english: He felt deeply ashamed after the teacher caught him slacking off.
example.fact: Blushing is one of the few human expressions Charles Darwin called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions' because no other animal is known to do it involuntarily. It is triggered by adrenaline widening the tiny veins in the face, and studies show people trust a blushing person more, since the reaction is almost impossible to fake.

examples.hanzi: 我考试作弊被抓,觉得非常羞愧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kǎoshì zuòbì bèi zhuā, juéde fēicháng xiūkuì.
examples.english: I was caught cheating on the exam and felt deeply ashamed.

examples.hanzi: 你不用羞愧,谁都会犯错。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yòng xiūkuì, shéi dōu huì fàncuò.
examples.english: There's no need to feel ashamed; everyone makes mistakes.

components.note: 民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 政府决定听取民众的意见。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ juédìng tīngqǔ mínzhòng de yìjiàn.
example.english: The government decided to listen to the opinions of the populace.
example.fact: Ancient Athens ran the world's first large-scale direct democracy around 500 BC, where roughly 6,000 citizens could gather in the Assembly to vote directly on laws by show of hands. Ordinary citizens were also chosen by lottery, not election, to fill most government posts, a system meant to prevent any single faction from controlling public office.

examples.hanzi: 民众对这座新桥感到非常满意。
examples.pinyin: Mínzhòng duì zhè zuò xīn qiáo gǎndào fēicháng mǎnyì.
examples.english: The public is very pleased with the new bridge.

examples.hanzi: 许多民众在街上庆祝新年。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō mínzhòng zài jiē shàng qìngzhù xīnnián.
examples.english: Many people celebrated the New Year in the streets.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 保护幼崽是动物的本能。
example.pinyin: bǎohù yòuzǎi shì dòngwù de běnnéng.
example.english: Protecting their young is an instinct in animals.
example.fact: Sea turtle hatchlings dig out of their sand nests and crawl straight toward the ocean within minutes of birth, without ever having seen water or a parent to guide them. Researchers believe they read the natural slope of the beach and the brighter horizon over open water, an instinct so fixed that artificial lighting near beaches can fatally misdirect them inland.

examples.hanzi: 听到巨响,他本能地蹲了下来。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào jùxiǎng, tā běnnéng de dūnle xiàlái.
examples.english: On hearing a loud bang, he crouched down instinctively.

examples.hanzi: 婴儿出生后就有吃奶的本能。
examples.pinyin: Yīng'ér chūshēng hòu jiù yǒu chī nǎi de běnnéng.
examples.english: Babies have an instinct for feeding from birth.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees; 梅 is the plum tree, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
每 (měi) gives the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 悔 huǐ and 海 hǎi.

example.hanzi: 冬天梅花开了。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān méihuā kāi le.
example.english: The plum blossoms bloom in winter.
example.fact: 梅 flowers in cold weather, making plum blossom a symbol of resilience. It belongs to the "Four Gentlemen" of art (梅兰竹菊: plum, orchid, bamboo, chrysanthemum). 梅雨 is the early-summer rainy season.

examples.hanzi: 公园里的梅花开得很好看。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ de méihuā kāi de hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: The plum blossoms in the park are lovely.

examples.hanzi: 她爱喝酸梅汤。
examples.pinyin: Tā ài hē suānméitāng.
examples.english: She loves sour plum drink.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 这个消息大大提高了大家的信心。
example.pinyin: zhège xiāoxi dàdà tígāo le dàjiā de xìnxīn.
example.english: This news greatly boosted everyone's confidence.
example.fact: The Richter scale for earthquakes is logarithmic, so each whole-number increase represents roughly 32 times more released energy, not merely a linear jump. That is why a magnitude 7 earthquake is not just 'a bit bigger' than a magnitude 6, but releases about 32 times as much energy — a difference vast enough to turn a shaking building into a collapsing one.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法大大节省了我们的时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ dàdà jiéshěngle wǒmen de shíjiān.
examples.english: This method saved us a great deal of time.

examples.hanzi: 他的汉语比去年大大进步了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ bǐ qùnián dàdà jìnbù le.
examples.english: His Chinese has improved enormously since last year.

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks seeing and watching, as in 看, 眼, 睡; 督 is to oversee, to watch over.
叔 (shū) is a loose hint for dū.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: to look carefully inside.
祭 (jì) is a loose sound clue for chá; 祭 also sounds out 际 jì and 擦 cā.

example.hanzi: 海关督察每天检查进出港的货物。
example.pinyin: hǎiguān dūchá měitiān jiǎnchá jìnchūgǎng de huòwù.
example.english: Customs inspectors check incoming and outgoing cargo every day.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was never a single continuous fortification but a patchwork of walls built by different dynasties over roughly 2,000 years, and it relied on a dense network of watchtowers where guards used smoke signals by day and fire by night to relay warnings of approaching threats across hundreds of miles.

examples.hanzi: 检查组的督察昨天来学校检查了。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎnchá zǔ de dūchá zuótiān lái xuéxiào jiǎnchá le.
examples.english: The inspector from the review team came to the school yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 上级会派人来督察工作进展。
examples.pinyin: Shàngjí huì pài rén lái dūchá gōngzuò jìnzhǎn.
examples.english: The higher-ups will send someone to supervise the progress of the work.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 蔬 are vegetables, as in 菜 vegetable, 草 grass.
疏 (shū) gives the exact sound.
艹 (grass) — plants; 菜 is vegetables, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
采 (cǎi) is the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 彩 cǎi and 踩 cǎi.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天都会买新鲜的蔬菜。
example.pinyin: māma měitiān dūhuì mǎi xīnxiān de shūcài.
example.english: Mom buys fresh vegetables every day.
example.fact: Tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers are botanically fruits since they develop from a flower's ovary and contain seeds, yet in 1893 the US Supreme Court ruled in Nix v. Hedden that tomatoes count as vegetables for import-tariff purposes, based on how they are commonly eaten rather than their botanical classification.

examples.hanzi: 多吃蔬菜对身体好。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Eating more vegetables is good for your health.

examples.hanzi: 这家超市的蔬菜又新鲜又便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāoshì de shūcài yòu xīnxiān yòu piányi.
examples.english: The vegetables at this supermarket are fresh and cheap.

components.note: 彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 工程师花了三天时间修复了系统漏洞。
example.pinyin: gōngchéngshī huāle sān tiān shíjiān xiūfù le xìtǒng lòudòng.
example.english: The engineer spent three days fixing the system vulnerability.
example.fact: The Sistine Chapel ceiling restoration, completed in 1994 after over a decade of work, revealed that centuries of candle soot and old varnish had darkened Michelangelo's frescoes so much that restorers had misjudged his palette for generations — the cleaned colors turned out to be far brighter and more vivid than anyone expected.

examples.hanzi: 师傅把那张老照片修复得很好。
examples.pinyin: Shīfu bǎ nà zhāng lǎo zhàopiàn xiūfù de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The craftsman restored that old photo very well.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机文件坏了,你能修复吗?
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī wénjiàn huài le, nǐ néng xiūfù ma?
examples.english: My phone file is corrupted; can you repair it?

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢画画。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan huàhuà.
example.english: He has liked drawing ever since he was little.
example.fact: Mozart began composing his first pieces of music at age five, and by age six he was performing for European royalty on tours arranged by his father. Modern research on child prodigies suggests such early starts often combine unusual working memory with thousands of hours of deliberate practice packed into the earliest years of life.

examples.hanzi: 我们从小就是好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cóngxiǎo jiù shì hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: We've been good friends since we were little.

examples.hanzi: 她从小在乡下长大,很会做农活。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo zài xiāngxia zhǎngdà, hěn huì zuò nónghuó.
examples.english: She grew up in the countryside and is good at farm work.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.

example.hanzi: 他把行李箱装满了礼物。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ xínglixiāng zhuāngmǎn le lǐwù.
example.english: He filled the suitcase with gifts.
example.fact: A camel can drink up to 200 liters of water in about three minutes when it finally reaches a water source, rapidly filling its bloodstream and rehydrating tissues that lost significant water weight during its trek. Contrary to popular belief, camels do not store water in their humps — the humps hold fat, which the animal metabolizes for energy on long desert journeys.

examples.hanzi: 我把背包装满了书和零食。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ bēibāo zhuāngmǎnle shū hé língshí.
examples.english: I filled my backpack with books and snacks.

examples.hanzi: 这辆卡车装满了水果,准备运往城里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng kǎchē zhuāngmǎnle shuǐguǒ, zhǔnbèi yùnwǎng chéng lǐ.
examples.english: This truck is loaded full of fruit, ready to be taken to the city.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
曼 (màn) — long, graceful; as a part it sounds out 慢 màn, 漫 màn, 馒 mán and 蔓 màn.

example.hanzi: 阿曼位于阿拉伯半岛的东南部。
example.pinyin: Āmàn wèiyú Ālābó bàndǎo de dōngnánbù.
example.english: Oman is located in the southeastern part of the Arabian Peninsula.
example.fact: Oman's Jebel Shams canyon is sometimes called the 'Grand Canyon of Arabia,' plunging roughly 1,000 meters, and the country still uses an ancient irrigation system called aflaj, dating back over 1,500 years, that channels water from mountain springs and underground sources to farms using only gravity.

examples.hanzi: 阿曼的沙漠和海滩都很有名。
examples.pinyin: Āmàn de shāmò hé hǎitān dōu hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: Oman's deserts and beaches are both famous.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友下个月要去阿曼出差。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou xià gè yuè yào qù Āmàn chūchāi.
examples.english: My friend is going to Oman on a business trip next month.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 叫, 吗; 吓 is a shout that frightens.
下 (xià) — same sound — 吓 is xià, like 下.
口 (mouth) — scaring with a shout; also in 叫 shout, 吓 frighten.
虎 (hǔ) gives the exact sound — a tiger's roar. In 吓唬 it reads xià hu.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢吓唬弟弟，说房间里有鬼。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuan xiàhu dìdi, shuō fángjiān lǐ yǒu guǐ.
example.english: He likes to scare his younger brother by saying there's a ghost in the room.
example.fact: Opossums have one of the most famous fear responses in nature: when threatened, they involuntarily collapse, drool, and emit a foul odor while appearing dead for up to several hours, a reflex called thanatosis. It is not a conscious act but an automatic nervous-system shutdown triggered by extreme stress, similar to fainting.

examples.hanzi: 别吓唬小孩子,他会做噩梦的。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiàhu xiǎoháizi, tā huì zuò èmèng de.
examples.english: Don't scare the little kid; he'll have nightmares.

examples.hanzi: 他戴着面具来吓唬我,可我一点也不怕。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàizhe miànjù lái xiàhu wǒ, kě wǒ yìdiǎn yě bú pà.
examples.english: He came to scare me wearing a mask, but I wasn't afraid at all.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 俄 first meant sudden, and is now mostly 俄国 Russia.
我 (wǒ) — near sound — 俄 is é; 我 also sounds out 鹅 é and 饿 è.

example.hanzi: 他会说俄语，也会说英语。
example.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Éyǔ, yě huì shuō Yīngyǔ.
example.english: He speaks Russian and English.
example.fact: 俄 is short for 俄罗斯 (Russia), a transliteration of Rossiya: 俄语, 俄国. In classical Chinese it also meant "suddenly," as in 俄而.

examples.hanzi: 他想去俄罗斯旅游。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù Éluósī lǚyóu.
examples.english: He wants to travel to Russia.

examples.hanzi: 我的同事在学俄文。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì zài xué Éwén.
examples.english: My colleague is learning Russian.

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).

example.hanzi: 他是这方面的专家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè fāngmiàn de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is an expert in this area.
example.fact: 专 means focused on one thing: 专业 (major, profession), 专家 (expert), 专心 (to concentrate), 专门 (specifically), 专利 (patent). 专车 is also a ride-hailing service.

examples.hanzi: 这位医生是心脏方面的专家。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshēng shì xīnzàng fāngmiàn de zhuānjiā.
examples.english: This doctor is a heart specialist.

examples.hanzi: 他读书很专心。
examples.pinyin: Tā dúshū hěn zhuānxīn.
examples.english: He is very focused when he reads.
